title: URAMP program terms: the out-of-practice period and return to practice during participation
rule_summary: The URAMP Guidance Manual describes practice during participation as follows. It states that all admissions carry an out of practice consideration: participants entering URAMP for a complaint based on a substance use disorder normally require a restriction from practice for the first six months in the program, with gradual return to work privileges granted as they continue to meet the program compliance criteria, while the duration of the restriction from practice for a complaint based on mental health functioning is determined by the URAMP admission evaluator and/or the rehabilitation evaluation committee; for mental health admissions the manual states that the program avoids fixed standards, including the length of time away from work. Under the heading Return to Practice Requirements the manual states that practice privileges shall be restored by the program prior to returning to practice, that return to practice requires a supervisor agreement and quarterly supervisor employment reports, and that, if required by the agreement, one year of health professions practice is required to successfully discharge from the program. Under Application for UCAP Changes, a participant requests a change to the URAMP Consent Agreement for Participants in writing on the required form; changes are considered only once the participant has demonstrated compliance with all the agreement's provisions and documentation requirements and only at the timeframes the agreement specifies; all changes must be reviewed and approved by URAMP staff or the rehabilitation evaluation committee; and the requests listed as applicable to all participants include, normally, a return to practice after six months of successful compliance under a substance use disorder agreement, a return to practice after a period out of practice as determined by the admission evaluator and/or the committee, and the return of practice restricted privileges as outlined in each agreement. Under Management of Disciplinary Matters, Step Four, after pending related complaints are dismissed on effective enrollment the licensing board authorizes the URAMP director to change the license status in accordance with the terms of the agreement and URAMP's staff action policy. Under Confidentiality Upon Successful Completion of the Program, the manual states that the URAMP legislation requires any change to a licensing restriction or condition to be approved by the participant's licensing board, and that where URAMP staff or the committee has approved a return to practice, with or without restrictions, during or at the conclusion of the program, the recommendations are put before the licensing board for final approval, without the participant's personal identifiable information. A participant must receive written approval from the URAMP program coordinator before practicing in a new practice setting, and may request to be heard before the committee for reconsideration of practice restrictions that are a significant barrier to practicing where the organization can offset or accommodate the barrier.
exam_relevance: Tests that the program's no-practice status on application does not mean a participant stays out of practice for the whole agreement: the manual describes a usual six-month restriction under a substance use disorder agreement, an individually set restriction for a mental health complaint, restoration of privileges by the program under a supervisor agreement, and final approval by the licensing board.

numeric_facts.fact: usual restriction from practice at the start of participation
numeric_facts.conditions: for a participant entering URAMP for a complaint based on a substance use disorder, as the manual describes it; for a complaint based on mental health functioning the admission evaluator and/or the rehabilitation evaluation committee determines the duration

numeric_facts.fact: health professions practice required to discharge successfully
numeric_facts.conditions: only if required by the participant's agreement

exceptions: For a complaint based on mental health functioning the manual sets no fixed period out of practice; the admission evaluator and/or the rehabilitation evaluation committee determines the duration of the restriction.
common_confusions: The non-disciplinary restriction status that attaches on application does not mean the participant stays out of practice for the whole five-year agreement; the manual describes practice privileges being restored by the program during participation.
Six months is described as the normal restriction under a substance use disorder agreement, not a guaranteed return date; return depends on continuing compliance and approval.
URAMP staff or the rehabilitation evaluation committee approve a return to practice within the program, but the manual describes the licensing board as giving final approval.
